hero_subtitle: Club policies, codes of conduct & coach expectations
intro: The policies below govern participation in every Jackson Soccer Club program. Players, parents, and coaches are expected to read and follow them. Select a policy to read the full text.

policies.title: Refund Policy
policies.body:
It is the policy of Jackson Soccer Club to refund registration fees only if your player moves more than 20 miles from his/her primary residence prior to the start of the season, or if the player is unable to participate due to a season ending injury or illness as documented by a physician.

No refunds, credits or fee transfers will be allowed for any other reasons. If Jackson Soccer Club is unable to place your child on a team, a full refund will be issued. Conflicts with practice schedules are not grounds for refunds. Refund requests due to injury must be made within 2 weeks of the injury or illness and must have a physician's note included. There will be no reimbursements granted for any programming canceled due to weather, acts of God, or forfeits.

policies.title: Uniform Policy
policies.body:
Jackson Soccer Club's official apparel and equipment sponsor is Puma. This relationship is critical to the success of both on and off-site programming. As such, all uniforms, training gear, cold weather gear, bags and training should be Puma branded.

Players registered to JSC Recreational or Competitive teams must purchase a uniform and training gear package at the beginning of the season from our retail partner, soccer.com. Players are required to wear appropriate JSC issued gear to each training session and game. There are no exceptions to this policy. Players are responsible for upkeep of this gear. Continuing players will have the opportunity to reuse last year's uniform if it is in the current style.

Competitive uniform purchases happen on a 2 year cycle on odd years (U11, U13, U15, and U17). New uniforms must be purchased on a 2-year cycle regardless of need. Uniform numbers will be assigned by the JSC competitive programs.

policies.title: Registration Fee Policy
policies.body:
Players will ONLY be allowed to participate with Jackson Soccer Club's organized leagues if one of the requirements below has been met:

- Player participation fees have been paid in full prior to the first scheduled game.
- Participation fees have been partially paid prior to the first scheduled game with a payment plan in effect.
- A registration waiver has been approved by the Jackson Soccer Club.

Unless otherwise communicated, all participation fees must be paid in full by the first scheduled game, unless on a payment plan.

Jackson Soccer Club will make an effort to collect past due fees as appropriate, with potential for removal of current and future playing privileges. Please remember that JSC is a nonprofit organization that survives off registration fees. Not paying fees as indicated could result in increased playing costs for all players.

Competitive Programs

After a player commits to a competitive team and completes the registration, the player is considered registered to the Jackson Soccer Club. Each player is bound to the Club for the entire seasonal year, which runs from August 1 of one year through July 31 of the following year. Families have the option of paying in full at the time of registration, or choosing a payment plan which allows the total to be divided equally into installments. The first payment must be made by the registration deadline. Each family is obligated to the full financial commitment, regardless of the choice made.

policies.title: Player Code of Conduct
policies.body:
A. Player Responsibilities

Participation in Jackson Soccer Club is a privilege, not a right. By registering with JSC, players agree to uphold the following standards of conduct to promote responsibility, respect, and good sportsmanship:

- Play for enjoyment, not solely to satisfy others. Strive to improve individual and team skills through consistent effort and focus.
- Learn, understand, and respect the laws of the game and follow them at all times.
- Show courtesy and respect to coaches by listening and following directions.
- Respect game officials. Refrain from questioning or commenting on their decisions during or after games.
- Show sportsmanship by treating opposing teams, coaches, and players with respect at all times, especially after a match.
- Maintain self-control. Avoid abusive or profane language, taunting, gestures, or physical aggression.
- Treat teammates, opponents, coaches, officials, and spectators with dignity and respect at all times.
- Wear the complete and proper uniform and gear to all practices and games, including shin guards and appropriate footwear. Bring water and avoid wearing jewelry for safety reasons.
- Help keep fields and facilities clean. Treat all practice and game environments with care, as you would your own home.
- Always carry proper identification and wear the appropriate uniform during games.
- Attendance is essential. Emergencies are understood, but consistent participation is expected. Notify JSC promptly if an issue arises. Chronic absenteeism may result in removal from the program.
- All players must attend annual evaluations each spring for team placement in the following season.
- Coaches reserve the right to move players to a different team based on ability, attitude, or club needs to ensure the best development environment.

B. Social Media Guidelines

Players must use social media responsibly and respectfully. The following rules apply:

- Do not share the location or any photos from inside private spaces (e.g., hotel rooms) during team travel.
- Never post profanity, hate speech, or racial slurs - whether or not they mention JSC.
- Refrain from making negative comments about players, coaches, parents, or clubs (including opponents).
- Do not criticize officials, tournaments, leagues, or event organizers online.
- Avoid any negative commentary about Jackson Soccer Club, its coaches, players, staff, or families.
- When sharing or commenting on JSC-related posts, maintain respectful language and tone.
- Positive posts highlighting JSC activities, games, or players are encouraged. Tag JSC when appropriate.

C. Anti-Bullying

Jackson Soccer Club is committed to providing a safe and respectful environment for all participants. Bullying in any form will not be tolerated and will be addressed promptly.

Bullying is defined as unwanted, aggressive behavior that involves a real or perceived power imbalance. The behavior is repeated or has the potential to be repeated over time. (Source: stopbullying.gov)

Types of bullying include verbal (insults, threats, or derogatory language), social or relational (spreading rumors, exclusion, or damaging reputations), and physical (harming someone's body or possessions).

Any player found bullying another individual will be subject to immediate dismissal from Jackson Soccer Club.

D. Enforcement

Violations of this Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, up to and including permanent removal from JSC programs and activities. All infractions will be reviewed by the club. Suspensions or removals due to conduct violations are not grounds for registration fee refunds.

E. Injury Reporting & Health Responsibility

Jackson Soccer Club places a high priority on the health and safety of all players. Players are expected to take personal responsibility for managing their health and well-being in the following ways:

- Players must report any injuries, illnesses, or symptoms to their coach or trainer immediately - before, during, or after games and practices.
- Players should not attempt to play through serious pain or injury without clearance from a qualified medical professional.
- If diagnosed with a concussion or any condition requiring rest, players must follow return-to-play protocols as directed by healthcare providers and JSC guidelines.
- Players are expected to stay hydrated, maintain proper nutrition, and get adequate rest to support performance and recovery.
- If a player requires medication (e.g., asthma inhaler, EpiPen), it must be discussed with the coach prior to the season or as soon as the need arises.

policies.title: Parent Code of Conduct
policies.body:
Youth soccer is for the players. All parents associated with the Jackson Soccer Club are invited to share in the pleasure of watching their children participate in the world's most popular sport, so long as their behavior does not distract the players and officials from the free flow of play which is the trademark of the sport. Jackson Soccer Club prides ourselves on having respectful and engaged families, and we ask that parents and guardians continue to adhere to these guidelines.

A parent or guardian should:

- Foster an environment of respect for referees, players, coaches, and spectators of the opposing team through words of encouragement and support.
- Applaud superior play, effort, and sportsmanship by players on both teams.
- Support your coaches and managers consistently regardless of the results on the field. Coaches contribute many hours of their time to your children. They deserve your congratulations when the team wins and your encouragement when the team doesn't.
- Communicate any concerns to the coach at the appropriate time (a 24 hour cool off period is recommended) away from the playing location and players.
- Always remain at least two yards from the playing field so our young players have room to play and enjoy the game.

Your cooperation with these standards before, during, and after each game or practice will make JSC more enjoyable for everyone.

A parent or guardian must:

- Never use foul language or obscene gestures at a game or practice site.
- Avoid comments and gestures that express disagreement with referee decisions.
- Cooperate with any request by the game officials.
- Never consume alcoholic beverages on the field location at practices or games.

A parent or guardian understands that:

- Any parent or spectator who fails to adhere to these standards will be required to leave the playing area, and play will be suspended until he or she does so.
- The JSC reserves the right to suspend or terminate a player's enrollment for his or her parent's persistent or extreme sideline misbehavior, and there will be no refunds of player fees in such cases.
- Parents or guardians are responsible for their guests' behavior and must inform their guests of the applicable rules of conduct.

Any breaches of this Code of Conduct can result in your child's suspension and a member's removal from the Jackson Soccer Club. Comments and behavior of any member which contradict the mission statement or disrupt the functioning of a team can result in the suspension and/or removal from the Jackson Soccer Club.

policies.title: Anti-Bullying Policy
policies.body:
The Jackson Soccer Club (JSC) is committed to providing players a fun, positive, and secure environment in which to learn and enjoy the game of soccer. We do not tolerate bullying at any practice, game or other JSC sanctioned event. We will promote a TELLING atmosphere. This means that anyone who knows that bullying is taking place is expected to report the incident. Players and parents should be assured that they will be supported when bullying is reported.

Definition of Bullying

Bullying is defined as conduct, gestures or comments which are insulting, intimidating, humiliating, hurtful, malicious, degrading or otherwise offensive to a player, group of players and/or teammates, and which create a hostile or intimidating environment, or which negatively affect a player's physical and/or emotional well-being. Bullying is any written, verbal or physical act, or any electronic communication, whether it is a single incident or a series of incidents, that results in intentional pain and distress to the victim.

Signs and Symptoms

A child may indicate he or she is being bullied through various signs and symptoms. While some children are prone to report bullying to their parents, coaches or adults, others will not, due to fear, intimidation or other factors. Coaches and parents should be aware of possible signs indicating that bullying may be taking place. These signs and behaviors could indicate other problems, but bullying should be considered a possibility and should be investigated.

Procedures for Parents, Coaches, and the Executive Board

Parents should report bullying incidents to the team coach or manager. If the problem persists, reach out to the JSC Executive Board. If necessary and appropriate, police may be consulted.

In all cases of reported bullying, parents of the player who was bullied shall be informed immediately and may be asked to meet with the respective team coach and/or executive member to discuss the incident. In all cases, strict confidentiality shall be maintained. It is not our goal to make a public example of reported incidents.

The negative behavior must be investigated and the bullying stopped immediately. The parents of any player who is reported to be bullying will be contacted immediately by the respective team coach, overall commissioner, or JSC Executive Board and asked to meet to discuss the incident to help the bully or bullies change their behavior.

Consequences of Bullying

In a first offense situation involving bullying, an attempt will be made to encourage the bully (or bullies) to modify their behavior for their benefit, for the benefit of the person bullied, and for the team. An attempt will be made by the coach, manager, or parent(s) to reconcile the situation between players (age and level of maturity and/or severity of offense must be considered).

If the bullying persists, disciplinary action against a player may be taken by the team coach and/or JSC Executive Board which may include, but is not limited to, immediate suspension from participation in practices or games for a period of time.

After the incident or incidents have been investigated and addressed, the situation will continue to be monitored by the respective team coach, team manager, and players' parents to ensure the problem is resolved.

policies.title: Conflict Resolution Policy
policies.body:
Jackson Soccer Club encourages our members to take a 24-hour "cool down" period before addressing a conflict that may have occurred. Complaints and concerns regarding your soccer experience should be directed according to the following guidelines.

Complaints regarding Jackson Soccer Club coaches, assistant coaches, and/or managers should be addressed with the head coach. If resolution is not satisfactory, document your concerns in writing to the attention of the appropriate program commissioner.

Concerns regarding your child's team should be addressed directly with your child's coach or assistant coach at a proper time and place. If resolution is not satisfactory, document your concerns in writing to the attention of the appropriate program commissioner.

If, after following the appropriate measures as listed above, resolution is not satisfactory, document your concerns in writing to the attention of the Jackson Soccer Club President.

Complaints and concerns regarding Jackson Soccer Club's player development policies, programs and coaching staff should be documented in writing and sent to the attention of the Jackson Soccer Club President and proper program commissioner.

Complaints and concerns regarding Jackson Soccer Club's administrative policies should be documented in writing and sent to the attention of the Jackson Soccer Club President.

policies.title: Coach Expectations
policies.body:
All members of the Jackson Soccer Club coaching staff are to see themselves as role models and ambassadors for the Club. We ask that our coaches be aware of how they represent themselves, their team, and Jackson Soccer Club. It is imperative that our coaches are respectful to all around them including parents, opposing teams, and referees. We expect our coaches to exhibit professional behavior at all times, both on and off the field. Disciplinary action will be taken against any member of the coaching staff whose actions bring the Club into disrepute.

Jackson Soccer Club coaches should aspire to be experts in player development and seek feedback and education, both formal and informal, that will help them down that path. We provide a variety of educational opportunities and resources for our coaches, including the coaching portal, to help our coaches be the best they can be. We ask that our coaches prepare for trainings by reviewing the session and curriculum materials provided. Jackson Soccer Club coaches must embrace the JSC philosophy and take pride in the development of each individual player assigned to them. We are committed to building a consistent style of play across our programming with the help of our dedicated coaches.

policies.title: Coach Sideline Policy
policies.body: Jackson Soccer Club has a zero-tolerance policy regarding aggressive coach sideline behavior. Excessive coaching is strongly discouraged and only positive reinforcement should be provided to our players by coaches and sideline spectators. Coaches will be removed from the program for consistent violations of this philosophy. There should be no negative interactions between coaches and referees, coaches and opposing coach/players, or coaches and visiting parents.

policies.title: Coach Right to Terminate
policies.body: The Jackson Soccer Club reserves the right to remove any volunteer coach or paid coach for any reason at any time. Additional action may be required if necessary, including banning coaches from attending games as spectators and removing any future coaching rights. If coaches refuse to cooperate, they and their children may be banned from the club immediately and possibly permanently. Any further refusal to cooperate can result in police interaction.

policies.title: Coach Right to Refuse
policies.body: Jackson Soccer Club reserves the right to refuse any coaches for any reason, except for reasons of race, color, national origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity, religion, reprisal, political beliefs, marital status, familial or parental status, sexual orientation, or if all or part of an individual's income is derived from any public assistance programs. Most importantly, the majority of reasons include perpetual negative or abusive sideline behavior.
